sections.hypothesis: Tori Trades' trendline method, long only and made mechanical, beats holding the same coin at the same average exposure after costs on BTC, ETH and SOL 4h bars: buy a close above a falling line through swing highs it touched at least 3 times, with no profit target, and leave on a close below the new rising line through the swing lows since the break.
sections.rationale: Asked for by Luke (2026-11-21) after reviewing her method (her videos; Tradezella and FXReplay's write-ups). Disclosed: a chart-pattern strategy, a family our entry bar rejects, and Kestrel has already dropped two trendline rules on BTC and ETH 4h (a falling-trendline breakout lost money while a plain breakout made money; a rising-trendline bounce did worse than without the line). What is new here: her three-touch requirement and her exit (no target; a trailing trendline), where the earlier tests used a fixed 3R target. Who pays: no clear payer; the honest case is that a break of a well-tested line triggers stop orders and trend-followers (the same under-reaction trend following rests on). Outside evidence: weak; Lo, Mamaysky and Wang (2000, Journal of Finance, 'Foundations of Technical Analysis') find some chart patterns carry slight information; her own record ($5,000 to over $500,000 in 11 years) is self-reported and unverified. Not tradable as she trades it: her shorts and most of her markets (commodity futures) aren't on Binance spot. The holdout is spent for BTC, ETH and SOL, so a pass could only be judged forward. Implementation: tori-trendline (kestrel.strategies.tori). Runs: 3 scorecard runs (3 trials), then the scorecard's neighbours and walk-forward, each counted.
sections.rules: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT 4h, each on its own, 2020-01 (SOL 2020-08) to 2025-10, through the bracket engine. Swing highs and lows of 3 bars each side, known only once confirmed (3 bars later). Resistance: a falling line through the latest known swing high B and the most recent earlier, higher swing high A (at most 180 bars before B) such that at least 3 swing highs from A to B lie within 50% of an ATR of the line, and no close was above it from A until the signal. Entry: a close above the line (any amount), one attempt per line; bought at the next open. Stop: the lowest low since B. No target. Exit: a close below the rising line through the two latest known swing lows formed since B (the later higher), sold at the next open; until that line exists the stop protects. Sizing: the bracket engine's fixed risk (risk% of equity over the distance to the stop, capped at 100%; she sizes by fixed risk). Long only.
sections.falsification: The full scorecard (CLAUDE.md), each coin: (1) Sharpe beats the coin held at the same average exposure, after costs; (2) deflated Sharpe >= 95%; (3) walk-forward: most windows beat exposure-matched holding; (4) at least half the 2-year start windows beat it; (5) break-even cost >= 2x actual; (6) at least 30 trades; (7) max drawdown <= 50%; (8) neighbours (swing_bars 2 and 4; min_touches 2 and 4; touch 25% and 75% of an ATR) also pass test 1; (9) net expectancy per trade beats 95% of random-entry paths with the same stops, exits and sizing (kestrel random-entry). If it passes every test but luck on at least 2 of the 3 coins, Claude recommends watch (judged forward on paper, the holdout being spent); otherwise drop. Luke decides either way.
sections.parameters: swing_bars 3, min_touches 3, touch_atr_pct 50, breakout_atr_pct 0 (her 'break of the trend': any close above), max_line_bars 180 (30 days of 4h bars). Fixed before any run; the neighbours above are tried and counted.
sections.costs: kestrel.toml: 7.5 bps taker fee (BNB discount), each coin's half-spread, square-root impact, Binance's 5 USDT minimum. 4h bars trade more often than our daily strategies; the break-even cost test checks that costs don't eat it.
